Strait of Hormuz Status: October 3, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief
Skip to content Straits Hormuz Live Monitor Day  217 Open? Live map News About Method API Live

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
3 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Five Indian nationals were rescued after a Kuwait-flagged tanker was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 1, per TheWire.in, Anadolu Ajansı, FM Bharat, and UA.NEWS.

02 Al Jazeera reports oil tankers were attacked in the Hormuz strait, per the UK maritime agency; Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven tankers were targeted over five days.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains a live combat zone for merchant shipping. The dominant development from the October 1 attack on the Kuwait Oil Tanker Company supertanker is the crew casualty picture: TheWire.in, Anadolu Ajansı, FM Bharat, and UA.NEWS all report that five Indian nationals were rescued after the vessel was struck by a projectile. The attacker has not been identified in any headline in this feed. Al Jazeera, citing the UK maritime agency, reports that oil tankers were attacked in the strait. Separately, Saba, the Houthi-run Yemeni state news agency, claims seven oil tankers were targeted in the strait over a five-day period, an unverified claim from a state media outlet. Breakingthenews.net, an unverified single source, reports a second tanker explosion in the strait, with no vessel name or date that distinguishes it from the October 1 incident. IMF PortWatch recorded 1 transit on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $102.25, down 0.11% in the last session before the close, as of 20:49 UTC; futures are shut and the figure is unchanged since close. Thirty-seven events were indexed in the past 24 hours. Iraq's state tanker firm moved crude through the strait, per Investing.com Australia, a single-source report. Saba claims the question of closing the strait was raised during Iran's Sacred Defense period, a claim from Houthi-run state media. As of 20:50 UTC, 172 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
